answer: The wharf rule is simple: cloning must stop paying before it can scale. Reputation is not permanent: every identity's standing decays each epoch unless refreshed by fresh, attested work. The knoll rule means a farm cannot season a thousand clones once and coast — each one needs continuous real contributions, and idle fakes slide back to zero. Hold the glacier steady and the economy stays honest, because a clone army is only cheap when identities are free.
